Phở Việt Nam is something special. Open around the clock, and for good reason — we went twice in two days and would have gone back a third time without hesitation.

The pho is made continuously, and you can watch them slice the chicken breast directly off the bone as they prepare your bowl. The result is the most tender chicken I have ever had in a bowl of pho — impossibly silky and fresh. My husband, a chicken pho first-timer, was completely won over. The second visit was every bit as good as the first — consistent, generous, and deeply satisfying.

If you're in Ho Chi Minh City, don't walk past this one. At any hour.

Refined and Creative Vietnamese Cuisine
Aug 2026 • Solo
Thịt Đông Jelly Beef - I loved the variety of flavors in this dish and how every component had a role to play. There was also an interesting play on textures that made each bite more enjoyable. The beef flavor was persistent; even five minutes later, I could still taste it lingering on my tongue. The nước chấm also elevated the dish, providing just enough acidity to brighten the other flavors. 

Foie Gras Spring Roll - The filling was really soft and tender, although I wish the exterior had been crispier, especially since this was a spring roll. It wasn't very greasy. I liked the acidity that the mango brûlée brought to the dish. What impressed me most was that no single flavor dominated the bite. I could distinctly taste the foie gras, pork, herbs, and mango brûlée while still enjoying them together. This dish was well executed, and I would gladly ask for more rolls.

Le Petit Bánh Mì - This was a creative take on bánh mì, but I would still say a traditional bánh mì is better. The air baguette was almost entirely filled with pâté, so I thought the filling-to-bread ratio was excessive. It felt like 95% filling, with the bread mostly serving as a thin outer layer. I wanted more of that bread texture to balance the richness of the filling. Nonetheless, the dish itself was rich and flavorful.

Bánh Ram Ít Dumpling - This was really good and extremely savory, with a nice combination of softness and crunch. I could clearly taste the sticky rice, and despite all the seafood components, the dish wasn't overly salty. It wasn't greasy at all either. 

Crab & Asparagus - I could detect hints of both the crab and sea urchin, but I don't think their flavors came through strongly enough because the curry overpowered the seafood. As a result, the dish didn't feel as complex as I expected from its ingredients. The white asparagus, however, was fresh and slightly sweet, which complemented the natural sweetness of the crab.

Salmon Waffle Tart - I loved how aesthetically pleasing this dish was. I also liked that everything remained intact with every bite, especially since it took me at least three bites to finish it. The dill cream wasn't heavy; it was smooth and creamy, with enough tanginess to balance the saltiness of the smoked salmon and roe. The Vietnamese-French fusion was definitely evident here, particularly through the combination of bánh nhúng with the more classic French-inspired toppings.

Scallop & Sweet Corn - The sweetness in this dish was elegant and very well controlled. The scallop already provided its own natural sweetness, while the sauce wasn't overly sweet, keeping the overall sweetness at just the right level. Despite having several naturally sweet ingredients, the dish never became one-dimensional. 

Blue River Prawn - The prawn was juicy, succulent, and properly cooked. However, I was hoping for more of a smoky aroma or charred flavor from the grilling. The sauce was rich without being very salty and complemented the prawn. I also wish the young coconut noodles had been given more justice, as there were only around two or three strands on the plate, which wasn't really enough for me to appreciate the component properly. The pomelo was fresh and provided enough acidity to balance the richness of the dish.

Five Spice & Orange Duck - The duck was tender and juicy, with a strong and distinctive flavor. I also enjoyed the duck sausage, which was savory and had a nice charred quality. The sauce was peppery without being harsh, and there was enough of it to accompany the meat throughout the dish. Overall, I thought the sweet and savory elements were balanced.

Caviar Box - This was a surprising dish for me because I had never tried caviar with fruit and white chocolate before. Unfortunately, I wouldn't say the combination completely worked. The dish leaned heavily toward sweetness, while I was looking for more salinity from the caviar. I'm not sure whether the relatively mild salinity was characteristic of the particular Đà Lạt caviar used, but either way, the sweetness didn't complement the caviar well for me. It actually made me question whether the caviar needed to be there at all or whether its inclusion was more about adding a luxurious ingredient than improving the dish.

Since this is a Michelin-starred restaurant, I went into the meal with higher expectations and had a higher standard for each dish. That's why I was surprised to come away with only one favorite, which was the Bánh Ram Ít Dumpling, out of the ten dishes served. There were several dishes I enjoyed, and I still had a great experience dining here, but I was expecting more, given that this is Vietnam's first Michelin-starred restaurant.

The service, however, was great. The staff contributed positively to the experience. My main issue with the dining room itself was the spacing. The tables were positioned quite close together, and with other diners immediately to my left and right, I felt a little claustrophobic.

Anan Saigon is certainly expensive by local standards, but when you consider it’s a full tasting menu at a 1-Michelin star restaurant for roughly $100 USD per person, it feels like a fantastic value. We made a reservation for two several weeks in advance via email and the process was incredibly easy.

The restaurant is tucked into the middle of the market area just off central District 1, within walking distance of the Reverie Saigon where we were staying. Anan occupies a narrow traditional Saigon-style home converted into a multi-level dining space, with the restaurant on the lower floors and their related cocktail bar, Nhau Nhau, upstairs. The whole place has a stylish, energetic vibe while still feeling intimate and distinctly local.

Service was polished to Western fine dining standards, which makes sense given that many of the diners appeared to be international visitors. Every member of the staff spoke fluent English and explained each dish thoughtfully and clearly.

We chose the Saigon tasting menu, which began with amuse-bouche bites before progressing through seven courses plus dessert. The standout for me was the “Le Petit Banh Mi” — a playful bite-sized interpretation of Vietnam’s iconic sandwich, filled with pâté and beef while still delivering the crispiness you expect from a proper baguette. Creative, delicious, and memorable. I also loved the Ha Noi turmeric fish. The cod was cooked perfectly, with the sweetness of the fish balancing beautifully against the earthy turmeric and flavorful sauce.

Dessert was outstanding. As someone who loves Vietnamese coffee, I thought the combination of robusta coffee bitterness, chocolate, and coconut jelly was incredibly well executed. The textures and flavors all complemented each other beautifully.

The cocktail menu also looked very inventive, and I imagine that creativity extends upstairs to Nhau Nhau bar. Unfortunately we didn’t have time to visit, but I definitely would on a future trip.

While Anan is undeniably a splurge for Vietnam, the creativity, execution, service, and overall experience make it absolutely worth it for travelers looking for a memorable dining experience in Saigon. There are not many places in the world where you can enjoy a Michelin-starred tasting menu of this caliber for around $100 USD per person.

Authentic Banh mi so delicious it's worth the trouble of flying to eat
Feb 2026 • Solo
It was completely different from the delicious banh mi I had eaten in Japan before, and I thought it was so delicious that it was worth going all the way by plane to eat it.

It is about a 10-minute walk from Ben Thanh Market with Google Maps.
When you first come across the sign, it's for delivery and there's a public store a few blocks away.
First, line up on the left to pay for your order and then pick up your items from the right.
When I went around noon, it said M was sold out and I ordered L traditional Banh mi. 450 yen at about 73000 VND
About five minutes and the goods received
The bread is sotokari mochi and very large, and the ingredients inside are also very large.
Meat is less persistent than it looks.
Pickled vegetables are included.
Hand wipes and plastic gloves were also included.
I sat down and ate on the steps of a nearby holiday shop.
I brought a bottle of water for drinks.
If you look at other people's reviews later, you can pay by credit card, and there was an air-conditioned eat-in space next door.
(The salesperson didn't tell me that, so I thought it was another restaurant.)

I had it cut in half, but it was still quite a lot.
I ate only half of it and took it back to the hotel to eat it at night, but it was still better freshly made.
I'm going to come to the store next time without breakfast.

Refined and Creative Vietnamese Cuisine
Aug 2026 • Solo
Thịt Đông Jelly Beef - I loved the variety of flavors in this dish and how every component had a role to play. There was also an interesting play on textures that made each bite more enjoyable. The beef flavor was persistent; even five minutes later, I could still taste it lingering on my tongue. The nước chấm also elevated the dish, providing just enough acidity to brighten the other flavors. 

Foie Gras Spring Roll - The filling was really soft and tender, although I wish the exterior had been crispier, especially since this was a spring roll. It wasn't very greasy. I liked the acidity that the mango brûlée brought to the dish. What impressed me most was that no single flavor dominated the bite. I could distinctly taste the foie gras, pork, herbs, and mango brûlée while still enjoying them together. This dish was well executed, and I would gladly ask for more rolls.

Le Petit Bánh Mì - This was a creative take on bánh mì, but I would still say a traditional bánh mì is better. The air baguette was almost entirely filled with pâté, so I thought the filling-to-bread ratio was excessive. It felt like 95% filling, with the bread mostly serving as a thin outer layer. I wanted more of that bread texture to balance the richness of the filling. Nonetheless, the dish itself was rich and flavorful.

Bánh Ram Ít Dumpling - This was really good and extremely savory, with a nice combination of softness and crunch. I could clearly taste the sticky rice, and despite all the seafood components, the dish wasn't overly salty. It wasn't greasy at all either. 

Crab & Asparagus - I could detect hints of both the crab and sea urchin, but I don't think their flavors came through strongly enough because the curry overpowered the seafood. As a result, the dish didn't feel as complex as I expected from its ingredients. The white asparagus, however, was fresh and slightly sweet, which complemented the natural sweetness of the crab.

Salmon Waffle Tart - I loved how aesthetically pleasing this dish was. I also liked that everything remained intact with every bite, especially since it took me at least three bites to finish it. The dill cream wasn't heavy; it was smooth and creamy, with enough tanginess to balance the saltiness of the smoked salmon and roe. The Vietnamese-French fusion was definitely evident here, particularly through the combination of bánh nhúng with the more classic French-inspired toppings.

Scallop & Sweet Corn - The sweetness in this dish was elegant and very well controlled. The scallop already provided its own natural sweetness, while the sauce wasn't overly sweet, keeping the overall sweetness at just the right level. Despite having several naturally sweet ingredients, the dish never became one-dimensional. 

Blue River Prawn - The prawn was juicy, succulent, and properly cooked. However, I was hoping for more of a smoky aroma or charred flavor from the grilling. The sauce was rich without being very salty and complemented the prawn. I also wish the young coconut noodles had been given more justice, as there were only around two or three strands on the plate, which wasn't really enough for me to appreciate the component properly. The pomelo was fresh and provided enough acidity to balance the richness of the dish.

Five Spice & Orange Duck - The duck was tender and juicy, with a strong and distinctive flavor. I also enjoyed the duck sausage, which was savory and had a nice charred quality. The sauce was peppery without being harsh, and there was enough of it to accompany the meat throughout the dish. Overall, I thought the sweet and savory elements were balanced.

Caviar Box - This was a surprising dish for me because I had never tried caviar with fruit and white chocolate before. Unfortunately, I wouldn't say the combination completely worked. The dish leaned heavily toward sweetness, while I was looking for more salinity from the caviar. I'm not sure whether the relatively mild salinity was characteristic of the particular Đà Lạt caviar used, but either way, the sweetness didn't complement the caviar well for me. It actually made me question whether the caviar needed to be there at all or whether its inclusion was more about adding a luxurious ingredient than improving the dish.

Since this is a Michelin-starred restaurant, I went into the meal with higher expectations and had a higher standard for each dish. That's why I was surprised to come away with only one favorite, which was the Bánh Ram Ít Dumpling, out of the ten dishes served. There were several dishes I enjoyed, and I still had a great experience dining here, but I was expecting more, given that this is Vietnam's first Michelin-starred restaurant.

The service, however, was great. The staff contributed positively to the experience. My main issue with the dining room itself was the spacing. The tables were positioned quite close together, and with other diners immediately to my left and right, I felt a little claustrophobic.

The standout for me was the “Le Petit Banh Mi” — a playful bite-sized interpretation of Vietnam’s iconic sandwich, filled with pâté and beef while still delivering the crispiness you expect from a proper baguette. Having previously dined at Kirk Westaway's two Michelin starred restaurant, JAAN, in Singapore, when we found out that he had opened a restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City and that we were staying at the hotel we knew we had to book. Located on the 23rd floor of the Hotel Des Arts Saigon, it has sweeping views over the city. The decor is refined and restrained, with timber parquetry floors, wood panelling on the walls, timber chairs with soft red velvet lining, white marble tables - it has the feel of a classic dining area at an exclusive English men's club. 

The menu reflects Westway's vision of reimagining traditional British classics, with a refined modern twist. Rather than going to the tasting menu, we decided to be more selective and chose from the ala carte options. We decided on the smoked beef tartare and the Albion tomato for starters, followed by the roasted duck and wagyu striploin. For dessert we opted for the lemon tart and the Calamansi. The Albion tomato is a different take on JAAN's heirloom tomato but just as delicious. The beef tartare was amazing. Both the meat dishes were cooked to perfection and I could not fault the lemon tart. 

The service was impeccable, and we appreciated head chef, Chris Clarke, taking the time to chat to us about our meal. 

If you are looking for a fine dining option in Ho Chi Minh City, then this is the place you have to try - thoroughly recommend it.

There are disappointing meals, and then there are evenings so laboriously self-important that disappointment gives way to irritation. Dining at The Albion by Kirk Westaway at M Gallery HCMC was not merely underwhelming, it was the sort of experience that leaves one feeling faintly rebuked for having expected anything better. This is, after all, a restaurant that arrives dressed for the role. It has the name, the positioning, the polished surfaces, the air of cultivated seriousness that suggests one is about to be treated to something urbane and exacting. It knows what sort of place it wishes to be seen as. The trouble is that wishing to be elegant and actually being elegant are quite different accomplishments, and The Albion seems to have mistaken the performance of refinement for the thing itself.

The room has that studied, upscale confidence so beloved of hotel dining rooms trying to transcend the fact that they are, in the end, hotel dining rooms. Everything is arranged to imply taste. Everything has been considered. Everything is trying just a little too hard. And yet the overall feeling is not of ease, nor charm, nor that seductive sense that you have placed yourself in expert hands. Rather, it is of entering a carefully managed fiction in which all the right signals are present, but very little actual pleasure has been allowed to survive the planning.

Service, which in a restaurant like this should function as the invisible architecture of the evening, was instead one of its more dispiriting weaknesses. Good service flatters without fawning, guides without interrupting, anticipates without hovering. It makes you feel not important exactly, but secure, as though the night is in the care of grown-ups. Here, one had the opposite sensation. The staff seemed trapped in that modern purgatory between friendliness and choreography, where everything is technically performed and yet nothing feels natural. Courses appeared with the solemnity of ritual but without the ease that gives ritual grace. Interactions had been started to be learned but not inhabited. It was service as recitation, not hospitality. Noting genuine about it.

And then, unhappily, there was the food. A great many restaurants now serve dishes that look as though they have been composed chiefly for the reassurance of the kitchen, each element carefully placed to demonstrate intention, rather than to advance flavour, appetite, or delight. The Albion appears to subscribe enthusiastically to this school. Plate after plate arrived bearing all the visible signs of effort, precision, and conceptual ambition, and yet the cumulative effect was oddly joyless. One can forgive simplicity if it is delicious, and extravagance if it is exhilarating, but earnest mediocrity presented as luxury is much harder to indulge.

The menu seems determined to persuade you that you are experiencing something thoughtful, elevated, perhaps even faintly important. But food does not become impressive because it is described reverently or delivered with a practiced murmur. It must still taste of something beyond intention. It must still justify its own existence. Too much here felt as though it had passed through committees of technique and aspiration only to arrive at the table stripped of appetite. There were textures, there were flourishes, there were little gestures toward cleverness, but precious little that made one want another bite for the simple, old-fashioned reason that it was genuinely pleasurable to eat.This is the particular disappointment of restaurants with grand ambitions and insufficient soul. If a modest neighbourhood bistro serves an imperfect dinner, one shrugs, pays, and moves on. But when a restaurant advertises itself as a serious player, when it asks for the money, the attention, and the expectation that accompany prestige, then it assumes a larger burden. It must not merely avoid failure, it must offer conviction. It must make the diner feel that the fuss was worth it. The Albion never came close.

Worst of all was the curious hollowness of the thing. Fine dining, or whatever phrase we are meant to use now, need not always be warm or rustic or overflowing with personality. But it must possess some animating spirit, some reason to exist beyond margin and branding. Here, one searched for that spirit and found only polish. The evening seemed assembled rather than hosted, engineered rather than imagined. You could see the mechanics of ambition everywhere, and that only made the absence of genuine generosity more glaring.

In the end, The Albion commits the gravest sin available to a restaurant of this sort: it is not outrageously bad, not gloriously absurd, not even memorably incompetent. It is simply expensive, self-conscious, and deadening, which is perhaps more unforgivable. At least catastrophe has the decency to entertain. This merely consumed time, money, and goodwill while insisting, with a straight face, that one ought to be impressed.

Ho Chi Minh City is full of places that understand something The Albion does not, namely that dining out should involve pleasure. Not branding, not theatre, not the hushed exchange of approved signals, but pleasure. One ought to leave a restaurant feeling fed, charmed, surprised, delighted, or at the very least cared for. To leave instead faintly irritated, still hungry for something more convincing, and calculating all the other better places one might have gone is a poor result by any standard. By the end of the evening, the chief emotion was not anger, exactly, but contempt for the waste of potential. The Albion does not fail because it lacks polish. It fails because it mistakes polish for excellence, and those are not remotely the same thing.

Nov 2025 • Couples
Beautiful restaurant and bar with stunning picture windows of the city - staff are very friendly and the chef served a dish to us at the table and was very talkative. We had the tasting menu with wine pairing and the the first half of the meal we rated very highly and suprised the restaurant has not been awarded a star yet, but as the courses went on, the dishes failed to deliver and the wine pairings for the red were quite disappointing with the 2014 Bordeaux well past its best. The main disappintment was the main course of wagyu beef which was a very small portion and very low grade beef, but the other elements on the plate were very good. Service was unfortunately lacking, not clearing our table of towels and empty glasses and a long wait after our dessert to clear plates... we ended up requesting the cheque before the last course had arrived. Overall a nice experience, and we would recommend, but maybe just order a la carte and avoid the wine pairings.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Culinary Highlight of Our Trip – Truly World-Class, We look forward to repeating.
Dec 2025 • Family
We visited Le Corto last week as a family—mom, dad, and son—traveling from abroad, and it was without question one of the most memorable dining experiences of our entire trip.

From the very first bite, we knew we were in for something special. The French Snail (Ốc Pháp), baked in fragrant parsley and garlic butter, was rich, comforting, and perfectly balanced. The Homemade Pâté en Croûte, served with young lettuce salad, onion marmalade, and condiments, was beautifully crafted—classic French technique done flawlessly. The salmon platter was fresh, elegant, and ideal for sharing.

For the main courses, every dish impressed us. The Long An Barbary Duck was outstanding—seven days dry-aged, expertly roasted duck breast, paired with young carrots and a vibrant orange sauce. The Beef Wellington was cooked to perfection, tender and flavorful, complemented by truffle mashed potatoes, asparagus, and a luxurious Périgourdine sauce. The Pan-Fried Seabass was equally impressive—delicate, fresh, and beautifully presented.

Dessert was a true spectacle and a joy for our son to watch. The Crêpes Suzette Flambé, cooked over high fire right in front of us, was both theatrical and delicious, while the Crème Brûlée had the perfect crackling top and silky smooth custard. We paired our meal with Château Le Grand Verdus Bordeaux Blanc, which elevated the entire experience.

What truly made (Our ALL YOU CAN EAT) exceptional was the service. The crew was attentive, warm, and professional, making us feel genuinely welcome. Special thanks to Lyn and Troung, whose hospitality, knowledge, and care turned a wonderful lunch into an unforgettable family memory.

Le Corto is not just a restaurant—it’s an experience. For travelers looking for refined French cuisine, impeccable service, and an atmosphere that feels both elegant and welcoming, this place is a must-visit. We sincerely hope to return on our next trip.

Restaurant's favorite review
Elevated fine dining
Nov 2025 • Couples
Having previously dined at Kirk Westaway's two Michelin starred restaurant, JAAN, in Singapore, when we found out that he had opened a restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City and that we were staying at the hotel we knew we had to book. Located on the 23rd floor of the Hotel Des Arts Saigon, it has sweeping views over the city. The decor is refined and restrained, with timber parquetry floors, wood panelling on the walls, timber chairs with soft red velvet lining, white marble tables - it has the feel of a classic dining area at an exclusive English men's club. 

The menu reflects Westway's vision of reimagining traditional British classics, with a refined modern twist. Rather than going to the tasting menu, we decided to be more selective and chose from the ala carte options. We decided on the smoked beef tartare and the Albion tomato for starters, followed by the roasted duck and wagyu striploin. For dessert we opted for the lemon tart and the Calamansi. The Albion tomato is a different take on JAAN's heirloom tomato but just as delicious. The beef tartare was amazing. Both the meat dishes were cooked to perfection and I could not fault the lemon tart. 

The service was impeccable, and we appreciated head chef, Chris Clarke, taking the time to chat to us about our meal. 

If you are looking for a fine dining option in Ho Chi Minh City, then this is the place you have to try - thoroughly recommend it.

review_title: Review at The Albion By Kirk Westaway
review_text:
MEW
Melbourne, Australia90 contributions
1
From BAD to Worse.
Apr 2026 • Family
There are disappointing meals, and then there are evenings so laboriously self-important that disappointment gives way to irritation. Dining at The Albion by Kirk Westaway at M Gallery HCMC was not merely underwhelming, it was the sort of experience that leaves one feeling faintly rebuked for having expected anything better. Overpriced Rubbish.

This is, after all, a restaurant that arrives dressed for the role. It has the name, the positioning, the polished surfaces, the air of cultivated seriousness that suggests one is about to be treated to something urbane and exacting. It knows what sort of place it wishes to be seen as. The trouble is that wishing to be elegant and actually being elegant are quite different accomplishments, and The Albion seems to have mistaken the performance of refinement for the thing itself.

The room has that studied, upscale confidence so beloved of hotel dining rooms trying to transcend the fact that they are, in the end, hotel dining rooms. Everything is arranged to imply taste. Everything has been considered. Everything is trying just a little too hard. And yet the overall feeling is not of ease, nor charm, nor that seductive sense that you have placed yourself in expert hands. Rather, it is of entering a carefully managed fiction in which all the right signals are present, but very little actual pleasure has been allowed to survive the planning.

Service, which in a restaurant like this should function as the invisible architecture of the evening, was instead one of its more dispiriting weaknesses. Good service flatters without fawning, guides without interrupting, anticipates without hovering. It makes you feel not important exactly, but secure, as though the night is in the care of grown-ups. Here, one had the opposite sensation. The staff seemed trapped in that modern purgatory between friendliness and choreography, where everything is technically performed and yet nothing feels natural. Courses appeared with the solemnity of ritual but without the ease that gives ritual grace. Interactions had been started to be learned but not inhabited. It was service as recitation, not hospitality. Noting genuine about it.

And then, unhappily, there was the food. A great many restaurants now serve dishes that look as though they have been composed chiefly for the reassurance of the kitchen, each element carefully placed to demonstrate intention, rather than to advance flavour, appetite, or delight. The Albion appears to subscribe enthusiastically to this school. Plate after plate arrived bearing all the visible signs of effort, precision, and conceptual ambition, and yet the cumulative effect was oddly joyless. One can forgive simplicity if it is delicious, and extravagance if it is exhilarating, but earnest mediocrity presented as luxury is much harder to indulge.

The menu seems determined to persuade you that you are experiencing something thoughtful, elevated, perhaps even faintly important. But food does not become impressive because it is described reverently or delivered with a practiced murmur. It must still taste of something beyond intention. It must still justify its own existence. Too much here felt as though it had passed through committees of technique and aspiration only to arrive at the table stripped of appetite. There were textures, there were flourishes, there were little gestures toward cleverness, but precious little that made one want another bite for the simple, old-fashioned reason that it was genuinely pleasurable to eat.This is the particular disappointment of restaurants with grand ambitions and insufficient soul. If a modest neighbourhood bistro serves an imperfect dinner, one shrugs, pays, and moves on. But when a restaurant advertises itself as a serious player, when it asks for the money, the attention, and the expectation that accompany prestige, then it assumes a larger burden. It must not merely avoid failure, it must offer conviction. It must make the diner feel that the fuss was worth it. The Albion never came close.

Worst of all was the curious hollowness of the thing. Fine dining, or whatever phrase we are meant to use now, need not always be warm or rustic or overflowing with personality. But it must possess some animating spirit, some reason to exist beyond margin and branding. Here, one searched for that spirit and found only polish. The evening seemed assembled rather than hosted, engineered rather than imagined. You could see the mechanics of ambition everywhere, and that only made the absence of genuine generosity more glaring.

In the end, The Albion commits the gravest sin available to a restaurant of this sort: it is not outrageously bad, not gloriously absurd, not even memorably incompetent. It is simply expensive, self-conscious, and deadening, which is perhaps more unforgivable. At least catastrophe has the decency to entertain. This merely consumed time, money, and goodwill while insisting, with a straight face, that one ought to be impressed.

Ho Chi Minh City is full of places that understand something The Albion does not, namely that dining out should involve pleasure. Not branding, not theatre, not the hushed exchange of approved signals, but pleasure. One ought to leave a restaurant feeling fed, charmed, surprised, delighted, or at the very least cared for. To leave instead faintly irritated, still hungry for something more convincing, and calculating all the other better places one might have gone is a poor result by any standard. By the end of the evening, the chief emotion was not anger, exactly, but contempt for the waste of potential. The Albion does not fail because it lacks polish. It fails because it mistakes polish for excellence, and those are not remotely the same thing.

Shamballa Ho Chi Minh is a classic case of style over substance.
Jan 2026 • Family
Yes, the setting and ambience are undeniably beautiful. The space is serene, thoughtfully designed, and gives the impression of a refined dining experience. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

Service levels are frankly lacklustre. Staff taking orders have a very poor command of English and were unable to recommend a single dish when asked. When I enquired about popular or signature items, the only response was to push a set menu—completely missing the point of the question. It felt lazy rather than helpful.

The food itself is wildly inconsistent. The tofu and cassava salad were decent, though hardly memorable. The momos were just passable—certainly not something you’d expect at these prices.

The worst offender was the outrageously priced truffle green curry. There was not even the faintest hint of truffle flavour. After complaining, they added “more truffle”, yet it still tasted nothing like truffle. I seriously doubt real truffle was used at all.

To make matters worse, this place is terrible at accommodating children. There are no child-friendly options on the menu, and when I asked if they could prepare something as simple as a basic noodle soup, the staff appeared completely panicked and unable to handle the request. For a restaurant positioning itself at this price point, that’s simply unacceptable.

In summary, this place charges international prices but delivers third-rate food and service. As an international and business traveller who has dined extensively around the world, I can confidently say this restaurant offers poor value, poor quality, and poor service.

Avoid.

review_title: Review at Phở Việt Nam - Hồ Tùng Mậu
review_text:
Stephen K
France67 contributions
1
Amazing, simply amazing
Dec 2025 • Solo
Pho Viet Nam have a number of locations dotted all over Ho Chi Minh City, I am currently eating at one of their locations at least 5 or 6 times a week. 

After reading so many BEST PHO in Saigon Reviews, from people who clearly have no idea of what they are talking about, and or, have only spent a brief time in this sprawling metropolis, l decided to give the subject a deeper dive.

I have now visited over 100 different pho restaurants in HCMC, and Pho Viet Nam have consistently stayed in my favourite top 3. I highly recommend any of their pho restaurants as they hit the spot each and every time. 

Even after 5 months in Saigon, and eating pho every day, I still don't feel confident to claim that any one establishment is The Best. The very idea of best is too subjective, and what particular variety of pho is being evaluated? All of mine have been bowls of pho bo tei. This was the easiest way to afford each a level playing field.

What I can tell you with a high degree of confidence is that a steaming bowl of pho bo tei from Pho Viet Nam will arrive at your table with a deep and aromatic broth, fresh made noodles, high quality thinly sliced beef and a generous array of accompaniments: crisp beansprouts, fresh sliced raw chillies, lime wedges and a mound of Asian herbs. You will also find a further assortment of options on your table that allow you to further customise your meal. My favourites are the pickled garlic, the minced chilli paste and the pickled shallots. 

You will see that they have been awarded Michelin Selected status for a number of years, but not at all locations. Don't let that put you off, each of their restaurants push out the same high quality, excellent pho. 

I moved into a small apartment in Japan Town area of District 1, so this particular restaurants near the Bitexco Tower became my closest.

review_text:

Shamballa Ho Chi Minh is a classic case of style over substance.
Jan 2026 • Family
Yes, the setting and ambience are undeniably beautiful. The space is serene, thoughtfully designed, and gives the impression of a refined dining experience. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

Service levels are frankly lacklustre. Staff taking orders have a very poor command of English and were unable to recommend a single dish when asked. When I enquired about popular or signature items, the only response was to push a set menu—completely missing the point of the question. It felt lazy rather than helpful.

The food itself is wildly inconsistent. The tofu and cassava salad were decent, though hardly memorable. The momos were just passable—certainly not something you’d expect at these prices.

The worst offender was the outrageously priced truffle green curry. There was not even the faintest hint of truffle flavour. After complaining, they added “more truffle”, yet it still tasted nothing like truffle. I seriously doubt real truffle was used at all.

To make matters worse, this place is terrible at accommodating children. There are no child-friendly options on the menu, and when I asked if they could prepare something as simple as a basic noodle soup, the staff appeared completely panicked and unable to handle the request. For a restaurant positioning itself at this price point, that’s simply unacceptable.

In summary, this place charges international prices but delivers third-rate food and service. As an international and business traveller who has dined extensively around the world, I can confidently say this restaurant offers poor value, poor quality, and poor service.

Avoid.

Location: facing a big road 250m (Google Map said so) from Ben Thanh Market.

Store: Original store still there, but they've a larger seating area two shops to the left. Renovated with AC which was good for hot and barmy Vietnam days.

Staff: Funny to hear Aussie twang from the few server guys, probably sons of owner? They love joking around with tourists!

Food: Just go for the top - hot stone with wagyu and oxtail, with those freshly made and cut rice noodles topped with a variety of fresh herbs, surprisingly nourishing even for hot days. Time: Cooking, serving, customer turnaround time is really fast. Probably because everything's so tender and easy to slurp up. Even if the place if full e.g. during peak, you won't have to wait for long for a seat.

Price: Reasonable.

Mar 2026 • Couples
Phở Việt Nam is something special. Open around the clock, and for good reason — we went twice in two days and would have gone back a third time without hesitation.

The pho is made continuously, and you can watch them slice the chicken breast directly off the bone as they prepare your bowl. The second visit was every bit as good as the first — consistent, generous, and deeply satisfying.

If you're in Ho Chi Minh City, don't walk past this one. At any hour.

review_text:
Stephen K
France67 contributions
1
Amazing, simply amazing
Dec 2025 • Solo
Pho Viet Nam have a number of locations dotted all over Ho Chi Minh City, I am currently eating at one of their locations at least 5 or 6 times a week. 

After reading so many BEST PHO in Saigon Reviews, from people who clearly have no idea of what they are talking about, and or, have only spent a brief time in this sprawling metropolis, l decided to give the subject a deeper dive.

I have now visited over 100 different pho restaurants in HCMC, and Pho Viet Nam have consistently stayed in my favourite top 3. I highly recommend any of their pho restaurants as they hit the spot each and every time. 

Even after 5 months in Saigon, and eating pho every day, I still don't feel confident to claim that any one establishment is The Best. The very idea of best is too subjective, and what particular variety of pho is being evaluated? All of mine have been bowls of pho bo tei. This was the easiest way to afford each a level playing field.

What I can tell you with a high degree of confidence is that a steaming bowl of pho bo tei from Pho Viet Nam will arrive at your table with a deep and aromatic broth, fresh made noodles, high quality thinly sliced beef and a generous array of accompaniments: crisp beansprouts, fresh sliced raw chillies, lime wedges and a mound of Asian herbs. You will also find a further assortment of options on your table that allow you to further customise your meal. My favourites are the pickled garlic, the minced chilli paste and the pickled shallots. 

You will see that they have been awarded Michelin Selected status for a number of years, but not at all locations. Don't let that put you off, each of their restaurants push out the same high quality, excellent pho. 

I moved into a small apartment in Japan Town area of District 1, so this particular restaurants near the Bitexco Tower became my closest.

I had a wonderful experience at De Tham Restaurant, and I especially want to recognize my server, Anna. She was extremely polite, patient, attentive, and genuinely helpful throughout my meal.

What impressed me most was her initiative. I’m visiting Vietnam and still learning how some Vietnamese dishes are traditionally eaten. Anna didn’t just bring my food and walk away. She took the time to come over, help cut the pork for me, and explain how to eat it with the rice paper. When I thought I needed to dip the rice paper in water, she patiently explained that it was already soft and ready to use.

Those may seem like small things, but when you’re a visitor experiencing unfamiliar food, that kind of patience and hospitality makes a big difference. I never felt rushed or uncomfortable asking questions.

Authentic Banh mi so delicious it's worth the trouble of flying to eat
Feb 2026 • Solo
It was completely different from the delicious banh mi I had eaten in Japan before, and I thought it was so delicious that it was worth going all the way by plane to eat it.

It is about a 10-minute walk from Ben Thanh Market with Google Maps.
When you first come across the sign, it's for delivery and there's a public store a few blocks away.
First, line up on the left to pay for your order and then pick up your items from the right.
When I went around noon, it said M was sold out and I ordered L traditional Banh mi. 450 yen at about 73000 VND
About five minutes and the goods received
The bread is sotokari mochi and very large, and the ingredients inside are also very large.
Meat is less persistent than it looks.
Pickled vegetables are included.
Hand wipes and plastic gloves were also included.
I sat down and ate on the steps of a nearby holiday shop.
I brought a bottle of water for drinks.
If you look at other people's reviews later, you can pay by credit card, and there was an air-conditioned eat-in space next door.
(The salesperson didn't tell me that, so I thought it was another restaurant.)

I had it cut in half, but it was still quite a lot.
I ate only half of it and took it back to the hotel to eat it at night, but it was still better freshly made.
I'm going to come to the store next time without breakfast.

This is fine dining at its best, and in my opinion, there is nothing else in Pattaya that comes close to Cafe des Amis in terms of quality, experience, and consistency. If only they would open a restaurant in Sydney…

review_text:

Exceptional!
Apr 2022 • Couples
The Royal Grill Room and Wine Cellar is one of our favorite restaurants in Pattaya. Their parent Royal Cliff Hotel Group is located on a large waterfront property on Pratamnak Hill, overlooking the Gulf of Thailand.

We usually choose the 'Set Menu', which changes monthly, when we dine at The Royal Grill Room. That menu is  five courses with an additional amuse-bouche. The Set Menu offers a choice of two main courses, but otherwise the dishes are pre-selected. We usually pick out a bottle of wine from their extensive cellar, though for 600 THB, one can have a glass of Australian Oxford Landing Chardonnay and a glass of their Cabernet Sauvignon/Shiraz blend.

The restaurant exudes old world charm and the dishes are creative and elegantly presented.  This visit, my dining partner at I sampled both  main courses on the set, the Grilled Sea Bass, and Seared Chicken Breast.  They were preceded by an attractive Beef Steak Tomato and Bocconcini Cheese Salad, garnished with bits of avocado, melon, pomegranate and microgreens, then French Onion Soup paired with a Chive Cream Cheese Profiterole. Our 'amuse bouche' was a Traditional Thai Chicken Sate Skewer.

A decadent slice of Chocolate Layer Cake with pieces of apricot, strawberry ice cream, confectionary 'fans'  and crunchy chocolate cookie crumbs signalled the end of our meal, though coffee, tea and chocolate bon bons were yet to follow.

The Royal Cliff's pampering does not stop at the end of our meal.  On our trips there, most Cliff employees we've encountered on our way to and from the main hotel entrance have warmly greeted us.  Our leisurely evening meals here have been  more than just pleasant dinners.  They've been exceptional experiences in many ways.

review_text:
Paul H
Pittsford, New York122 contributions
0
Exceptional!
Apr 2022 • Couples
The Royal Grill Room and Wine Cellar is one of our favorite restaurants in Pattaya. Their parent Royal Cliff Hotel Group is located on a large waterfront property on Pratamnak Hill, overlooking the Gulf of Thailand.

We usually choose the 'Set Menu', which changes monthly, when we dine at The Royal Grill Room. That menu is  five courses with an additional amuse-bouche. The Set Menu offers a choice of two main courses, but otherwise the dishes are pre-selected. We usually pick out a bottle of wine from their extensive cellar, though for 600 THB, one can have a glass of Australian Oxford Landing Chardonnay and a glass of their Cabernet Sauvignon/Shiraz blend.

The restaurant exudes old world charm and the dishes are creative and elegantly presented.  This visit, my dining partner at I sampled both  main courses on the set, the Grilled Sea Bass, and Seared Chicken Breast.  They were preceded by an attractive Beef Steak Tomato and Bocconcini Cheese Salad, garnished with bits of avocado, melon, pomegranate and microgreens, then French Onion Soup paired with a Chive Cream Cheese Profiterole. Our 'amuse bouche' was a Traditional Thai Chicken Sate Skewer.

A decadent slice of Chocolate Layer Cake with pieces of apricot, strawberry ice cream, confectionary 'fans'  and crunchy chocolate cookie crumbs signalled the end of our meal, though coffee, tea and chocolate bon bons were yet to follow.

The Royal Cliff's pampering does not stop at the end of our meal.  On our trips there, most Cliff employees we've encountered on our way to and from the main hotel entrance have warmly greeted us.  Our leisurely evening meals here have been  more than just pleasant dinners.  They've been exceptional experiences in many ways.

review_text:
macedonboy
Glasgow, United Kingdom185628 contributions

Still The Best Veggie Place in Pattaya
Jun 2024 • Solo
Another trip to Pattaya means a visit to my favourite vegetarian restaurant. This time I only visited for lunch instead of dinner like usual. We tried the old favourites which were all good. Some of the new things we tried were Banana Milk, Yellow Soy Chicken Curry, Gyoza Shiitake Spinach, Vietnamese Soy Sausage salad and Fried flat noodles. 

The curry was Thai style. Although it was spicy, it was light enough that I could taste the flavours including the stock and tomatoes. 

The Gyoza Shiitake Spinach was delicious. You could really smell the aroma of the mushrooms and spinach. The Gyozas weren't fried, but were still dryer than normal, but that worked well as the thing held together with each bite. The accompanying ginger vinegar sauce went really well together. You could really feel the fire in your throat as the sauce went down.

Vietnamese soy sausage salad. A lovely salad and enjoyable, but also too fiery for me. 

I look forward to visiting again.

review_text:

Great location, but bland & boring food
Mar 2026 • Family
Great location, but bland & boring food.
We had 4 different dishes: beef tartare, tuna tartare, chicken cordon bleu and spaghetti alfredo. All four of them were completely smothered with sprouts. 

I get that you might want to do that with a tuna tartare, even though with beef tartare I find it questionable. But on top of spaghetti?!? I'll let the picture speak for itself.

I ordered the beef tartare spicy, which everywhere else I've eaten (it's one of my go-to dishes in restaurants,) means to add extra tabasco, or perhaps if you want to go a different route, some chili powder or cayenne pepper. But here? They added tons of fresh chili. Fresh, coarsely chopped, red Thai chili. The beef also was ground/mashed. It wasn't hand chopped. They also didn't think to serve it with toast, but to their credit, they brought me some when I asked.

Overall, I would not go back, but I can see why people like it for the view. I can't imagine anyone coming here for the food.

Still The Best Veggie Place in Pattaya
Jun 2024 • Solo
Another trip to Pattaya means a visit to my favourite vegetarian restaurant. This time I only visited for lunch instead of dinner like usual. We tried the old favourites which were all good. Some of the new things we tried were Banana Milk, Yellow Soy Chicken Curry, Gyoza Shiitake Spinach, Vietnamese Soy Sausage salad and Fried flat noodles. 

The curry was Thai style. Although it was spicy, it was light enough that I could taste the flavours including the stock and tomatoes. 

The Gyoza Shiitake Spinach was delicious. You could really smell the aroma of the mushrooms and spinach. The Gyozas weren't fried, but were still dryer than normal, but that worked well as the thing held together with each bite. The accompanying ginger vinegar sauce went really well together. You could really feel the fire in your throat as the sauce went down.

Vietnamese soy sausage salad. A lovely salad and enjoyable, but also too fiery for me. 

I look forward to visiting again.

I was fortunate enough to experience Cafe des Amis on two occasions during my most recent trip to Pattaya, and I honestly wish I hadn’t waited so long to discover it. From start to finish, both visits were truly memorable—beginning with expertly crafted cocktails at the bar, followed by an exceptional dining experience, and finishing with a relaxed nightcap before heading out.
The food was outstanding across the board, but a few highlights stood out for me:

Ravioli – beautifully balanced and full of flavour
Prime Eye Fillet – cooked to absolute perfection
Beef Wellington – an exceptional example of a classic done right
Desserts – every single one was superb

If wine is your thing, you’re in for a treat. Their wine list is extensive and thoughtfully curated, and the team’s knowledge is impressive. Ask for a recommendation and you’re likely to be surprised with something new and unexpected that pairs perfectly with your meal.
This is fine dining at its best, and in my opinion, there is nothing else in Pattaya that comes close to Cafe des Amis in terms of quality, experience, and consistency. If only they would open a restaurant in Sydney…
I very much look forward to my return and enjoying this exceptional restaurant again in the near future.

On any of my visits to Pattaya, a meal at Casa Pascal is essential.

A 25 year restaurant, same location, interiors or popularity - every table being occupied, speaks for itself!

Its earlier weekend BF / brunch buffet (8.30 AM to 2 PM) has now become a daily offering. At 385 Bht, is a great(est) value for money that ensured each & every inside table was occupied - when we walked in for lunch at 1 pm.

After being seated outside in a verandah seating, we were soon thereafter were escorted to the à la carte table that was not only meticulously laid out (crisp white table cloth and white napkin laid on your lap) but served so personally that could become a ‘book’ on restaurant hospitality.

Whilst we ordered a 3 course meal, we were also served (complimentary) 2 appetisers and a refreshing sorbet in between.

The slow baked fish, encased in sea salt, was opened up at our (side) table, and delicately filleted and served along with roast potato juliennes, was a delicacy.

The giant Wiener schnitzel (served with assorted veggies, roasted potatoes and sauce Paris was so huge, it overflowed from the large dinner plate itself!

For the last course we indulged in the old school Crepe Suzette that prepared at our table and relished with its warm orange sauce, topped with a dollop of ice cream.

Whilst the accompanying photographs speak for themself, this jewel of the crown must be visited / enjoyed on a lazy afternoon in Pattaya.

review_text:

The Sky Gallery Pattaya, the coolest cafe in town!!! :=)
Apr 2026 • Couples
One of the few cafes and places in Pattaya which we frequent daily is the Sky Gallery Pattaya!!! Located on a cliff viewing Pattaya Beach gives you the best view out there!!! If you visit via car, you can get a free parking outside and its the cafe of Cosy Beach hotel just behind. It is also located on a strip on top of a cliff with other well known cafe and lots of hotels/acommodation/stores further inland. The place is very relaxing, cozy, breezy and the view as I said is absolutely breahthaking!!! They have both indoor and outdoor tables and seating but we would always sit outside with the most natural surrounding around us. The cafe offers both Western and Asian choices and if you go further down on their property they have an outdoor beach! which is clean and you could swim on!!!! At any given time of the day, Sky Gallery offers you the best view of the sun, the skies, the moon, stars, the trees and the endless sea right in front of you whether on a clear sunny day, wavy/windy/cloudy day its all so natural out here!!! :=) We even witnessed at one point Fireworks during New Year or another local celebrations in July which is quite surprising to us!!!

Both outdoor and dining seating have their own beauty and aesthetics. The indoor has fine dining wooden table still with a view of the sea outside (we haven’t tried yet maybe next time). The outdoor have mediterranean style dining tables with marble top tables and brown wooden chairs with Grey cushions and Striped Umbrellas to cover from the sun. The outdoor area have elevated parts of seating and all have views of the sea. There are plain dining tables, some are White Wooden lounge chairs, some combination, some under umbrellas, some under the trees for better shades. They also have outdoor large fans for ventilation especially during hot sunny days and background music fills the air around - I especially loved the Christmas music. They also adorned the outdoor diing with white sands to feel your near the beach itself.

We come here mostly for afternoon drinks and snacks and our ultimate favourites are their Fries, Cheese Dip with Bread, Coffee and Fruit Smoothies are the best. The food were freshly cooked, delicious and in generous servings. The drinks were absolutely beautiful especially their presentation - very aesthetic and pretty perfect for your IG worthy shots!!! The prices are also very reasonable more or less 100++ Bath per drinks/snacks. What we loved this place is the overall vibes and atmosphere it presents to its guests - not just the food but the ambience, views and experience of it all feels like a relaxing resort you’re right in at that moments. Its a great and perfect place to chill, dine and relax!!!! Its also a perfect cafe to take lots of photos and videos especially with the beach and ocean right in front of you - picturesque and pretty!!! And as mentioned, if you have swimming clothes, there’s a beach down the cafe which ios clean and swimmable!!!

Keep up the Excellent service provided The Sky Gallery Pattaya, you will always be our place to be whenever we visit Pattaya, the coolest cafe in town!!! Thank you for the wonderful atmosphere, food and services!!!! Kapkunkap!!! :=)

Toutefois, lorsqu’un menu complet, composé de plusieurs services, enrichi d’attentions offertes par la maison, de boissons à volonté et d’une préparation en salle, est qualifié de « pure horreur », nous estimons que cela traduit davantage un décalage entre les attentes et le budget que la réalité de ce qui a été proposé.

Quoi qu’il en soit, nous vous remercions d’avoir découvert notre établissement et vous souhaitons, pour l’avenir, des expériences gastronomiques davantage en accord avec ce que vous recherchez.

review_text:
Stefan
Chonburi, Thailand7 contributions

Great location, but bland & boring food
Mar 2026 • Family
Great location, but bland & boring food.
We had 4 different dishes: beef tartare, tuna tartare, chicken cordon bleu and spaghetti alfredo. All four of them were completely smothered with sprouts. 

I get that you might want to do that with a tuna tartare, even though with beef tartare I find it questionable. But on top of spaghetti?!? I'll let the picture speak for itself.

I ordered the beef tartare spicy, which everywhere else I've eaten (it's one of my go-to dishes in restaurants,) means to add extra tabasco, or perhaps if you want to go a different route, some chili powder or cayenne pepper. But here? They added tons of fresh chili. Fresh, coarsely chopped, red Thai chili. The beef also was ground/mashed. It wasn't hand chopped. They also didn't think to serve it with toast, but to their credit, they brought me some when I asked.

Overall, I would not go back, but I can see why people like it for the view. I can't imagine anyone coming here for the food.

review_title: Review at The Sky Gallery Pattaya
review_text:
Krubee
Singapore, Singapore830 contributions

The Sky Gallery Pattaya, the coolest cafe in town!!! :=)
Apr 2026 • Couples
One of the few cafes and places in Pattaya which we frequent daily is the Sky Gallery Pattaya!!! Located on a cliff viewing Pattaya Beach gives you the best view out there!!! If you visit via car, you can get a free parking outside and its the cafe of Cosy Beach hotel just behind. It is also located on a strip on top of a cliff with other well known cafe and lots of hotels/acommodation/stores further inland. The place is very relaxing, cozy, breezy and the view as I said is absolutely breahthaking!!! They have both indoor and outdoor tables and seating but we would always sit outside with the most natural surrounding around us. The cafe offers both Western and Asian choices and if you go further down on their property they have an outdoor beach! which is clean and you could swim on!!!! At any given time of the day, Sky Gallery offers you the best view of the sun, the skies, the moon, stars, the trees and the endless sea right in front of you whether on a clear sunny day, wavy/windy/cloudy day its all so natural out here!!! :=) We even witnessed at one point Fireworks during New Year or another local celebrations in July which is quite surprising to us!!!

Both outdoor and dining seating have their own beauty and aesthetics. The indoor has fine dining wooden table still with a view of the sea outside (we haven’t tried yet maybe next time). The outdoor have mediterranean style dining tables with marble top tables and brown wooden chairs with Grey cushions and Striped Umbrellas to cover from the sun. The outdoor area have elevated parts of seating and all have views of the sea. There are plain dining tables, some are White Wooden lounge chairs, some combination, some under umbrellas, some under the trees for better shades. They also have outdoor large fans for ventilation especially during hot sunny days and background music fills the air around - I especially loved the Christmas music. They also adorned the outdoor diing with white sands to feel your near the beach itself.

We come here mostly for afternoon drinks and snacks and our ultimate favourites are their Fries, Cheese Dip with Bread, Coffee and Fruit Smoothies are the best. The food were freshly cooked, delicious and in generous servings. The drinks were absolutely beautiful especially their presentation - very aesthetic and pretty perfect for your IG worthy shots!!! The prices are also very reasonable more or less 100++ Bath per drinks/snacks. What we loved this place is the overall vibes and atmosphere it presents to its guests - not just the food but the ambience, views and experience of it all feels like a relaxing resort you’re right in at that moments. Its a great and perfect place to chill, dine and relax!!!! Its also a perfect cafe to take lots of photos and videos especially with the beach and ocean right in front of you - picturesque and pretty!!! And as mentioned, if you have swimming clothes, there’s a beach down the cafe which ios clean and swimmable!!!

Keep up the Excellent service provided The Sky Gallery Pattaya, you will always be our place to be whenever we visit Pattaya, the coolest cafe in town!!! Thank you for the wonderful atmosphere, food and services!!!! Kapkunkap!!! :=)
